figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Schematic depicting strategies for the production of the plant-originated anti-cancer drug paclitaxel. 
Current approaches for producing paclitaxel involve the extraction of key precursors from Taxus plants or Taxus cell 
suspension cultures, followed by semisynthetic processes to produce paclitaxel. Alternatively, the heterologous 
expression of paclitaxel biosynthetic enzymes in microbial or plant-derived host systems enables the production of key
paclitaxel precursors or related taxane intermediates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Schematic of the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway. The yellow-green module depicts one proposed 
biosynthetic pathway leading to baccatin III, while the pink module represents an alternative biosynthetic pathway. The gray 
module indicates the postmodiﬁcation pathway involving the synthesis of the β-phenylisoserine side chain coupled to baccatin 
III. TXS: taxadiene synthase; T5αH: taxadiene-5α-hydroxylase; TAT: taxadiene-5α-ol-o-acetyltransferase; T10βH: taxane-10β-
hydroxylase; T13αH: taxane-13α-hydroxylase; T2αH: taxane-2α-hydroxylase; T9αH: taxane-9α-hydroxylase; T7βH: taxane-
7β-hydroxylase; T1βH: taxane-1β-hydroxylase; TBT: taxane-2α-o-benzoyltransferase; DBAT: 10-deacetylbaccatin III-10-o-
acetyltransferase; TOT: taxane oxetanase; BAPT: baccatin III-3-amino, 13-phenylpropanoyltransferase; T2′αOH: taxane-2′α-
hydroxylase; DBTNBT: 3′-N-debenzoyl-2′-deoxytaxol-N-benzoyltransferase; PAM: phenylalanine aminomutase; PCL:
β-phenylalanine CoA ligase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Schematic of diverse synthetic biology strategies for taxane biosynthesis. Various metabolic engineering 
strategies have been used to successfully redirect metabolic ﬂux toward the biosynthesis of taxanes. These strategies include 
enhancing the supply of taxane precursors, tunable control of taxane-related metabolic pathways, cell-free biochemical 
synthesis, and synthetic microbial consortia. In addition, CRISPR-based and RNAi-based strategies for regulating targeted 
gene expression and remodeling metabolic networks play crucial roles in overcoming bottlenecks in the de novo taxane 
biosynthetic pathway. The ER network has been shown to extend from the chloroplast, consistent with recent observations
demonstrating ER–choloroplast physical coupling during plant terpenoid synthesis [30]. The chemical and biological coupling 
scheme: PdII :  Pd  (OAc)2,  BQ:  p-benzoquinone. CRISPR: clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats; ER:
endoplasmic reticulum.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Schematic illustrating AI-driven advanced strategies for enhancing taxane biosynthesis. (A) Biosensor-
driven high-throughput screening: A genetic biosensor emits ﬂuorescence upon binding to the target taxane intermediate. A 
library of random mutants, derived from taxane biosynthetic genes, is generated and sorted using FACS according to 
ﬂuorescence intensity (high, moderate, or low). Key genes (e.g., gene a, gene b, gene c) involved in taxane biosynthesis 
are subsequently identiﬁed via NGS. (B) Schematic of the EvolvePro enzyme-evolution platform: the iterative workﬂow initi-
ates with low-throughput mutagenesis of target enzymes, where a pretrained PLM generates structural embeddings through 
residue-level feature extraction. Domain-speciﬁc representations are obtained by positional averaging across functional 
regions, subsequently training a regression model on experimentally validated activity data (K = batch size; f(x) = prediction 
score). Through active learning loops, top-performing mutants identiﬁed in each cycle (top n selection) feed back into PLM 
parameter updates, establishing a closed-loop optimization system, as denoted by dashed update arrows. (C) ML-assisted 
pathway optimization: pathway optimization progresses through three consecutive phases: (i) a design phase using Golden 
Gate assembly to modularize PRO-ORF-TER (POT) units; (ii) a testing phase quantifying product titers in phenotyped strain 
libraries under controlled fermentation; and (iii) an optimization phase deploying gradient-boosted regression models to
map conﬁguration-titer relationships, where prediction conﬁdence intervals guide combinatorial parameter adjustment.
This computational-experimental integration enables systematic reﬁnement of biosynthetic performance. AI: artiﬁcial
intelligence; FACS: ﬂuorescence-activated cell sorting; ML, machine learning; NGS: next-generation sequencing; ORFs:
open-reading frames; PRM: protein language model; PROs: promoters; TERs: terminators.
